newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria continues its rise in firm Brady market.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria continues its rise in firm Brady market.

text.p: Bulgarian Bradys pressed higher on Thursday in a generally firm emerging debt market, though there was some early morning profit-taking, traders said.

Bulgaria, the most volatile of the Bradys, has been relentlessy driving higher since late last month on the belief -- especially among speculators -- that the country is finally on the mend and no longer in danger of imminent economic ruin.
"There a bit of a tussle at the moment between profit-taking and investors trying to go overweight or neutral. But any pull-back will be well bid," a U.S. bank trader said.
IABs were bid in the morning at 57-3/8 cents in the dollar, up 3/4 of a point, though FLRBs dipped 1/4 of a point to 43-3/4.
Russia was also well bid but traders noted it was slightly below the all-time high of 84 cents for dollar paper touched late on Wednesday.
The rest of the market is firm with some interest in Philippine, with pars up 3/4 of a point at 90 cents.
One trader noted buying interest in the morning in Peruvian debt on talk that local pension funds will start buying the assets.
Peru PDI when and if bonds were up a point at 66.5 cents.
